question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

It is 2036. Looking back, 5 landmark papers each settled this question in a way that surprised the field, because of how they approached it. For each paper, describe what it measured, analyzed, or did, as a concrete idea a research lab could pursue today. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Degron timing: is AP-1 the ledger or the pen?
ideas.description: Tag FOS/JUN with auxin degrons, establish an AP-1-dependent cell state (e.g., drug-tolerant melanoma, activated fibroblasts), then degrade AP-1 after establishment while tracking accessibility, nascent transcription, and state markers hourly, with washout re-induction. A state that survives acute AP-1 loss but cannot be re-established shows AP-1 writes the memory without storing it.

ideas.title: Hysteresis curves instead of on/off experiments
ideas.description: Drive AP-1 with a dose- and duration-tunable synthetic input (inducible FOS-JUN dimer or optogenetic dimerizer) and map the full up-and-down dose-response of enhancer accessibility and target gene output. Memory becomes a measured quantity: the area of the hysteresis loop and the width of the bistable range, comparable across cell types.

ideas.title: Memory half-life measured per cell division, not per hour
ideas.description: Combine a live AP-1 activity reporter with lineage barcoding and continuous imaging so stimulus-induced state is followed through known numbers of mitoses in single lineages. Fitting decay of mother-daughter and cousin-cousin correlations separates dilution-by-division from time-dependent decay, distinguishing heritable chromatin memory from a merely slow protein.

ideas.title: Watching memory get rebuilt behind the replication fork
ideas.description: Use EdU-capture-coupled ATAC and CUT&RUN to ask, minute-by-minute after fork passage, whether AP-1 reoccupies its sites before accessibility returns or vice versa, and image AP-1 retention on mitotic chromosomes. The temporal ordering identifies the physical carrier of the memory rather than just its correlates.

ideas.title: Motif knock-ins that break recall but not response
ideas.description: CRISPR-mutate individual AP-1 motifs in candidate memory enhancers, in cells and in a mouse epithelium with wound or inflammatory memory, then assay the second stimulus rather than the first. A mutation leaving the naive response intact while abolishing faster/stronger recall is direct evidence that those sites are the memory element itself.
